RISK ASSESSMENT & FREQUENCY OF FOLLOW UP
 Risk category 
Parameters
Low
Medium
High
Follow up
Once a year
Once in 6 months
Once in 3 months
Callus alone, No LOPS, No PAD
Previous amputation or ulceration & 
any two of – Deformity/ LOPS/ PAD
Deformity with LOPS or PAD
DO:
• Daily self inspection of foot
∙ Wear comfortable proper ﬁtting footwear
∙ Cut toe nails straight
∙ Keep blood sugars controlled
∙ Regular foot check up with your doctor
DON’T:
• Walk barefoot, even at home
• Remove calluses/ corns at 
home
• Smoking: delays healing
PATIENT EDUCATION
DO:
∙ Moist dressings
∙ Change dressings 
daily for dirty wounds 
and on alternate days 
for clean wounds
DON’T USE:
• Hydrogen peroxide, EUSOL, povidone 
iodine, chlorhexidine etc
• Hyperbaric oxygen, antimicrobial 
dressings and stem cell therapy has 
insufﬁcient evidence to be 
recommended
WOUND CARE
1. ULCER
2. PERIPHERAL ARTERY 
DISEASE (PAD)
3. LOSS OF PROTECTIVE 
SENSATIONS (LOPS)
4. DEFORMITIES
INFECTION AND ANTIBIOTICS GUIDANCE
 No antibiotics
 At least two of: 
• Swelling/ induration 
• Pain/ tenderness
• Warmth, redness (0.5‐2cm) 
• Purulent discharge
• Redness 
• Deep tissues affected 
(abscess, osteomyelitis, 
fasciitis, septic arthritis) 
• No systemic signs
Local ﬁndings + systemic 
ﬁndings of SIRS (at least two 
of) 
• Temperature >38ºC or <36ºC, 
• Heart rate > 90/min, 
• Respiratory rate > 20/min or 
PaCO2 <32 mm Hg, 
• WBC >12000 or < 4000 or 
immature bands >10%
NON INFECTED WOUND
MILD INFECTION
SEVERE INFECTION
MODERATE INFECTION
Refer to higher centre
Give oral antibiotics for 1-2 
weeks
(Target only aerobic 
gram-positive cocci)
(Note: - Antibiotics are insufﬁcient unless combined with appropriate wound care)
Corns/callosity
Scaling in OPD
Footwear modiﬁcation
Web space fungal infection
Topical antifungals
Maintain local hygiene
Charcot’s foot
Refer to higher centre
MANAGEMENT OF OTHER RELATED FOOT CONDITIONS/ COMPLICATIONS
EVALUATION OF PATIENT WITH DIABETIC FOOT
ALWAYS KEEP A LOW THRESHOLD FOR REFERRAL TO HIGHER CENTRE
Standard Treatment Workﬂow (STW)
DIABETIC FOOT
ICD-10-Z86.31
RED FLAG 
SIGNS
 SYSTEMIC: Sick look, drowsy, abnormal breathing, abnormal pulse, fever
 LOCAL: Claudication/ rest pain, gangrene, osteomyelitis, acute charcot’s foot
Refer to higher centre
A. General condition 
1. Vitals 
2. Glycaemic control – FBS/ PPBS regularly, HbA1c once in 6 months
B. Local examination 
Check both feet for the below mentioned 
conditions
Ulcer
See for open infected wound
Check for osteomyelitis with bedside
probe-to-bone test or an X-ray
Also refer to higher centre with facilities for:
• Surgical debridement of wounds with necrotic tissue
• Cellulitis needing fasciotomy
• Wet gangrene needing amputation
• Cases needing negative pressure wound therapy
If osteomyelitis not suspected: 
• Do moist dressings
• Achieve good glycaemic control
• Off-load the foot
If osteomyelitis is 
suspected: 
Refer to higher centre for 
further management
Peripheral artery 
disease
• History of intermittent 
claudication,
• Absent pulsations in 
Posterior tibial artery 
and dorsalis pedis 
artery
• Ankle branchial index 
< 0.9
Refer to higher centre 
for further evaluation 
and consideration for 
revascularisation
Neuropathy/ loss of 
protective sensations 
(LOPS)
History of tingling, 
numbness,
“feels like walking on 
mattress”
Check for foot sensation 
using 10gm monoﬁlament
If sensations are absent 
and patient is 
asymptomatic, then 
educate the patient, 
advise protective footwear, 
and call for regular follow 
up as per risk category
Structural foot 
deformity
Look for gross 
deformities like 
• hammer toes
• claw toes
• hallux valgus
• pes cavus
• rocker bottom foot
Refer to higher 
centre
General conditions
• Older age
• Uncontrolled hyperglycemia 
• Duration of diabetes mellitus
• Peripheral artery disease
• Visual impairment 
• Chronic kidney disease
Local conditions
• Loss of peripheral sensations
• Structural foot deformity 
• Limited joint mobility
• Improperly ﬁtting footwear
• Callus
• History of ulcer/ amputation
